standard_prerequisites.name: The interval as a higher inductive type
standard_prerequisites.statement: The interval I is generated by 0 : I, 1 : I and seg : 0 = 1, with an induction principle and a recursion principle whose computation rules are definitional at the three constructors.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof builds maps I -> B and I -> (A -> B) by the recursion principle with prescribed values at 0, 1 and seg (source lines 411-417 and 418-419).

standard_prerequisites.name: Function extensionality may not be assumed here
standard_prerequisites.statement: For the duration of the proof the function extensionality axiom is suspended, so f = g in A -> B must be produced by an actual path.
standard_prerequisites.use: The conclusion at source line 422 is the path ap q (seg) in the function type, not an application of any extensionality axiom; the retained context supplies the suspension.

core_obligations: Start from p : prd x:A (f x = g x) and, for each x : A, define ptil_x : I -> B by the interval recursion principle with ptil_x(0) := f x, ptil_x(1) := g x and map ptil_x (seg) := p x (source lines 411-417).

Assemble the family into one map q : I -> (A -> B) by q(i) := (lam x. ptil_x(i)), which is again an application of the recursion principle, now with the function type as codomain (source lines 418-419).
Compute the two endpoints of q: q(0) is lam x. ptil_x(0), equal to f because ptil_x(0) is defined to be f x, and q(1) equals g for the same reason (source lines 420-421).
Read off map q (seg) : f = g in the type A -> B, which is the statement (source line 422).

proof_roadmap.step: For each x : A build ptil_x : I -> B by interval recursion from the given pointwise equality.
Package the family as a single map q : I -> (A -> B).
Identify the endpoints of q with f and g and conclude by ap q (seg).

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 6.3.2 at source lines 404-408: if f x = g x for every x : A then f = g in A -> B, and this is proved with the function extensionality axiom suspended. The proof is a real construction rather than a citation: for each x : A it builds ptil_x : I -> B by interval recursion, sending the path constructor seg to the given path p x (source lines 411-417), and then applies recursion a second time at the higher type I -> (A -> B) to obtain q (source lines 418-419). Both endpoint identifications at lines 420-421 rest only on the recursion computation rules, and the conclusion is the path ap q (seg) in the function type (line 422): nothing in the statement records that the interval's path constructor, and not any extensionality axiom, is what produces the function-level equality.
